decisions: Approvals are an OVERLAY, never a gate: approving/rejecting moves no stock and changes no source status. 0094 creates no function and no trigger, so the DB has no mechanism for it - keep it that way.

Completion = TWO MATCHING VOTES from distinct people. That is the only definition, shared by 0096's guard, 0097's trigger and the Ledger. 'One objection ends it' was tried and dropped because it could complete an event on a single vote.

0096 is scoped to consumption_approvals ONLY. The inventory approval tables are already locked at completion by their own RPCs (each gates on status='pending_approval'), so a trigger there would guard nothing while reaching into the stock-moving path.

0096's applied function bodies are byte-different from the migration file - inline comments were stripped in transit. Normalised (comments + whitespace) both hash identically, so the logic IS the file's. A future byte-comparison will trip on this; it is not drift.

Parts Usage falls back to work_order_parts.qty x unit_price_sar when a part has no per-lot ledger rows. Ledger-only aggregation silently dropped 57 of 78 consumed units (73%) because 2 completed work orders predate the ledger. The fallback is the SAME stamped figure from the other end of the same write.
work_orders.actual_cost_sar EQUALS the parts value exactly on all 13 deducted rows - never add it on top of parts consumption, it double-counts.
Archive linking: a linked document stores NEITHER its number nor its expiry; both live on the subject. 0092 moved that rule from the app into the database (raises 23514 rather than silently NULLing).

archive_linked_types and archive_one_linked_doc_per_person DO NOT EXIST - 0090 dropped that duplicate design. 0089/0091 on disk hold superseded versions and are EXPECTED to differ from live; do not 'fix' them to match.
Never let a linked identity column into an update payload from a form that renders it disabled - a disabled input submits nothing, which is how 04e3433 blanked iqama/licence on unrelated edits.
Customers get no Restore: 0019 archives a customer as a side effect of archiving its 1:1 project, so a solo restore would leave a half-restored state.
